name: Calvenza
blurb: Glassworks on the outer islands; its kilns light the lagoon at night and its glass is sold to every court.

name: Brenzolo
blurb: Salt-fish market where guild factors weigh every catch and quarrel over the price of eels.

name: Orsana Vara
blurb: Mint city of the Republic, where the guild treasury stores its gold behind iron doors.

name: Feltravo
blurb: Felt-and-wool town on the high canal; a legend says its first Provost drowned rather than sign a tariff.

name: Gaiazzo
blurb: Lombard hill-fort guarding the river pass, long contested by the Regency's marshals.

name: Torre Sallante
blurb: Tower of salt-merchants; its cellars hold the guild's debts written on cracked wax.

name: Pelagrino
blurb: Chapel-fortress where pilgrims pay tolls to cross; the monks keep the best ledgers in the land.

name: Ostrenga
blurb: Damp stone keep on a marsh island, rented out to mercenary companies by the season.

name: Montorzo
blurb: Hilltop castle whose lords refuse to pay canal tolls and sell their wine to the highest bidder.

name: Fiorvena
blurb: Garden castle with orchards irrigated by a Republic-built aqueduct; the Provost summers here.

name: Dolmare
blurb: Coastal fort at the lagoon mouth; its beacon warns merchant ships of Fen raiders.

name: Cavedina
blurb: Reed-cutters who sell thatch to every canal city; their feud with Fen boatmen is older than the Republic.

name: Brollo
blurb: Orchard village famed for pear brandy, shipped downriver in barrels stamped with guild seals.

name: Pozzale
blurb: Well-village where water-clerks test every cistern; they swear a curse lies in the deepest one.

name: Remigo
blurb: Oarmakers' village, its ash-trees felled and carved into the rowers of a thousand galleys.

name: Caldoro
blurb: Hot-spring village that sells bathing rights to merchants and heals no one who owes a debt.

name: Sciaretto
blurb: Fishing hamlet whose nets are tied with guild knots; its catch pays the Sorvelle locks.

name: Nevrone
blurb: Snow-fed mill village grinding grain for three cities, always short of millers and honest weights.

name: Gorgola
blurb: A whirlpool village at the river bend; sailors pray here before crossing the Ancaro sluices.

name: Stellaro
blurb: Lamp-makers' village; its oil lamps mark the canal routes and are sold across the Regency.

name: Pescaldo
blurb: Eel-catchers' village; they swear their eels are blessed and pay yearly tithes to the Pelagrino monks.

name: Mantesca
blurb: Dye-works village where cloth is coloured with woad and madder; its runoff tints the river blue.

name: Dorsolo
blurb: Gilded-mud village where prospectors wash silt for flecks of gold; they never share their claims.

name: Ravanelle
blurb: Market-garden village whose radishes and leeks feed Brenzolo's fish-market; a bitter rivalry.

name: Ciotto
blurb: Stone-quarry village whose masons built half the canal bridges; a strike here once froze trade for a year.

name: Bindaro
blurb: Rope-walk village where hemp is spun for every guild galley; each rope is knotted with a guild's name.

name: Ussaglia
blurb: Ferry village at the lagoon edge; ferrymen smuggle salt past the Republic's tolls each night.

name: Valgrana
blurb: Grain-valley village whose harvest pays the Republic's mercenary wages; its lords are sullen and proud.

name: Heeluma
blurb: Reed-boat yard where every clan's oath-stone is carved; its smoke-hung docks build the fastest hulls in the fen.

name: Kaarnesta
blurb: Stilt market on the black lake, famed for eel-smoked fish and a grudge against the river-guild toll-barges.

name: Ruunhaavi
blurb: Moot-island town where the oath-moot meets each midsummer; its bell is rung only when a clan breaks faith.

name: Liivanne
blurb: Salt-marsh shrine town trading peat-fire and amber; lords of the Salt-road still pay tribute here, grudgingly.

name: Lohvaara
blurb: Mazed reed-fort whose paths shift with the tide; a fabled trap that swallowed a Regency host.

name: Sooraalen
blurb: Ancient stilt-fort ringed by moss-walls; its keeper refuses any oath that names a king.

name: Veenhalla
blurb: Peat-brick hold on a sunken island; its cellars hold the clans' sworn reed-scrolls.

name: Kiivarra
blurb: Watchtower of oak piles over black water, guarding the only causeway into the heart of the fen.

name: Vaalikka
blurb: Half-sunken chapel-keep where the oath-moot's sacred eels are kept and fed each spring.

name: Nurmuun
blurb: Hill-fort of turf and stone above the reed line, a lookout against salt caravans from the south.

name: Hamaanne
blurb: Ruined ferry-castle whose toll chain was broken by river-guild marines; the clans want it back.

name: Akkeli
blurb: Eel-weir village whose traps feed half the fen; its fishers guard their weirs with knives.

name: Jaarvun
blurb: Hunting hamlet on the shore of Jaarvun Mere, famed for black-feathered decoy birds.

name: Sirreka
blurb: Smithy village working bog-iron into arrowheads; the Salt-road caravans once tried to buy every one.

name: Meelvi
blurb: Beekeepers hang hives on the reed-stalks here; a grudge with the forest wardens over stolen combs.

name: Otsuuk
blurb: Lakeside village known for whistle-songs that carry clan signals across three miles of mist.

name: Vihkuu
blurb: Ferryman's hamlet where river-guild surveyors vanished; locals still leave them offerings.

name: Ruokkaa
blurb: Fishing village on stilts, famed for its rope of twisted sedge that holds fast in any storm.

name: Tiiruus
blurb: Cairn-village marking the oath-moot's boundary; its stones are said to move when a clan lies.

name: Ylaaka
blurb: Upland hamlet of dry reed-thatch, a rare dry patch in the fen that bandits covet.

name: Kuolmi
blurb: Village of bone-pit ossuaries where clans bury their dead in the peat; the living avoid it at dusk.

name: Eepsaa
blurb: Crossroads hamlet where mud-roads meet the causeways; it sells passage for silver to any caravan.

name: Ohtaam
blurb: Reed-harvest village whose annual cutting festival ends in a mock raid on the nearest town.

name: Rimmaa
blurb: Quarry village of soft limestone; its masons build the only stone barges in the fen.

name: Mooraa
blurb: Wild-goose hunters' village; its geese are said to warn of approaching river-guild galleys.

name: Haapuu
blurb: Birch-grove village of shamans who read oath-omens from the bark of fallen trees.

name: Vesseli
blurb: Salt-marsh hamlet where caravan drovers once fled raiding clans; their hidden salt-caches are rumoured.

name: Gaiuuk
blurb: Mudflat village famed for its reed-boat racers; wagers here have started three feuds.

name: Khorvand
blurb: Holy city where the Pyre-Synod keeps the eternal brazier; its sulphur-scented hostels house pilgrims.

name: Dzelmasi
blurb: Obsidian-cutting town; its blades are blessed in the temple before they are sold to outsiders.

name: Tsarvik
blurb: Terraced market town famed for the black-vine wine that is never sold beyond the mountain.

name: Pyrgeti
blurb: Walled hill-town with hot springs; a grudge over a brazier stolen by canal guild agents.

name: Vardakar
blurb: Cliff fortress above the lava gorge; its gate-bell is rung only when the mountain speaks.

name: Kheshmund
blurb: Black-stone keep holding the oath-stone on which every priest-king is crowned.

name: Dzoravan
blurb: Siege-proof castle whose cisterns are fed by a hot spring that never freezes.

name: Ruvaskar
blurb: Border castle guarding the salt pass; a long feud with the caravan clans over its toll.

name: Tsitelgar
blurb: Mountain keep of ash-grey stone; its garrison has never surrendered in three sieges.

name: Mokheti
blurb: Frontier fort on the canal road; the guilds call it a thief's wall, the synod a holy shield.

name: Oghvarn
blurb: Castle built into a cooled lava tube, famed for its heavy armoured wardens.

name: Obrazi
blurb: Ash-farming village; its fields are famous for black barley grown on old lava.

name: Lekhvan
blurb: Shepherd hamlet whose flocks are sheared for the felt that lines the levies' helmets.

name: Tsoranik
blurb: Hot-spring village; bathers claim the water shows a ruler's fate.

name: Dvalisi
blurb: Quarry village cutting obsidian for temple altars; a grudge with Dzelmasi over prices.

name: Hrevaneth
blurb: Vineyard hamlet whose sour red wine is poured at every coronation.

name: Ghemurt
blurb: Mining hamlet on the slope; miners sing a hymn to the mountain before each shift.

name: Vezhari
blurb: Bell-founders' village; its bronze bells are said to quiet the mountain.

name: Kashvel
blurb: Pilgrim stop where the road climbs to the synod; pilgrims pay their toll in ash.

name: Nerzhi
blurb: Fishing hamlet on the black lake; the synod's clergy have cursed its nets.

name: Pakhvari
blurb: Treeless hill village famed for stone fire-shrines standing at every crossroad.

name: Ulgeti
blurb: Mule-breeding village that supplies the salt caravans; temple scribes despise it.

name: Sekhomi
blurb: Weaving village whose red cloth is worn by the priest-guards.

name: Ardzhan
blurb: Smoke-cured meat village; its hams are offered in the great temple each year.

name: Mirzhak
blurb: Woodcutter hamlet at the forest edge; a feud with the Warden villages over timber.

name: Tervani
blurb: Herb-gathering village; its healers are feared for their mountain-root poultices.

name: Fashgeti
blurb: Gate village below Oghvarn; locals pay their tithe by guarding the lava road.

name: Zorvenk
blurb: Ash-pit village where potters fire clay in volcanic kilns, known for black urns.

name: Brezhnik
blurb: Birch-bark tanners' market; every Warden's election is held under its great oak council tree.

name: Ostrogrado
blurb: Walled market-town where the Compact's oath-rolls are kept and feuds are settled by the bowstring.

name: Mirkovice
blurb: Honey and wax trading town, with a lingering grudge over a beehive tax the Regency tried to levy.

name: Lipnevo
blurb: Linden-wood carvers and bowyers; its yew-stave workshops supply half the Compact's longbows.

name: Hrastovec
blurb: Oak-ringed hillfort where the first Warden was chosen by a hunter's arrow.

name: Ukrenvar
blurb: Stone keep built by the Regency and now a Compact prize, held by a disputed garrison.

name: Vodnagrad
blurb: Lake fortress that refused the king's tax-collectors for three generations.

name: Ruzhovec
blurb: Rose-thorn hedge fort whose ditches are said to have been dug by the forest's own spirits.

name: Yasenvar
blurb: Ash-tree castle with a legend that its gate opens only for a Warden's true heir.

name: Stribogra
blurb: Wind-watch tower on the ridge; its keepers light beacons to warn the villages below.

name: Vezhdrak
blurb: Crumbling watchtower whose broken stair is a favourite ambush spot for outlaws.

name: Smrekovo
blurb: Spruce-resin village at the marsh edge, site of the disputed timber line with the Fen.

name: Hlivno
blurb: Mud-brick village famous for its clay ovens and the bread that feeds the Wardens' hunts.

name: Brusnice
blurb: Berry-picking hamlet where the pickers swear their oaths over cups of sour cider.

name: Dubnyak
blurb: Oak-cutters' village with a long feud against the Salt-road's timber caravans.

name: Zhelnice
blurb: Ironwood gatherers; a legend says the first bow of the Compact was carved here.

name: Oshnivo
blurb: Hunters' lodge village known for its hounds; a famous bear once killed a Regency marshal.

name: Kravnik
blurb: Cattle-breeders on the fen edge who still pay a yearly toll to the reed clans.

name: Tranok
blurb: Charcoal-burners' hamlet; the black smoke draws unwelcome riders in the dry season.

name: Mokrenka
blurb: Damp village built on stilts, with a grudge over a Warden who drowned in its millpond.

name: Volchyk
blurb: Wolf-trapper village whose pelts are prized in the River-guild cities, which overcharge them.

name: Redlice
blurb: Red-clay pottery village whose kilns scent the air for miles on festival nights.

name: Gorvenka
blurb: Mountain-pass hamlet where herdsmen once stopped an Ashland priest's procession.

name: Sedlov
blurb: Saddle-makers' village that sells fine horse gear to whichever lord pays best.

name: Bukhrov
blurb: Beech-wood hamlet with a shrine to the Hunter's Oath, carved into a living tree.

name: Lyutoda
blurb: Stone-bridge village where the river toll is collected by the Warden's sworn men.

name: Chorvena
blurb: Forest chapel village whose bell is rung backward when a Warden is slain.

name: Vrasnik
blurb: Crow-watch village whose scouts are trained to read the birds' warnings from the canopy.

name: Ondrac
blurb: Causeway town on the marsh edge, famous for its toll-gates and the grudge of Fen raids.

name: Pellegrane
blurb: Pilgrim-road town holding the mortgage deeds on half the royal granaries, owed to river bankers.

name: Corbanel
blurb: Wine-cellar town; the crown's last unpawned casks sleep under its market hall.

name: Tessaguel
blurb: Cloth market where dyed silks fetch lordly prices, and where guild factors count the regents' debts.

name: Ysembert
blurb: Sickroom fortress where the child-king sleeps under a dozen physicians' watchful eyes.

name: Castelnarc
blurb: Largest keep in the realm; its walls still bear the scorch marks of the Regents' War.

name: Montsorel
blurb: Hilltop castle whose lord claims the regency by right of his mother's blood.

name: Nerveille
blurb: Marshland castle guarding the causeway; its garrison is paid late and its keeper is often drunk.

name: Garrouse
blurb: Mountain keep with a gate of black oak and a legend of a knight who never came down.

name: Ombrelac
blurb: Lakeside castle whose moat is said to hold the drowned crowns of old kings.

name: Auberrac
blurb: Vineyard hamlet with a famous sour red that soldiers drink before every battle.

name: Pichelle
blurb: Mill village whose waterwheel is the regency's only dependable tax income.

name: Sanquerec
blurb: Chapel village where a miracle spring is said to cure the ailing king's fever.

name: Ganteil
blurb: Shepherd village known for glove-makers and a long feud with the nearby lord's pigs.

name: Roucalh
blurb: Quarry village supplying the great castles; its stonemasons strike whenever pay is late.

name: Vignebel
blurb: Orchard village; its cider is served at every regent's feast and blamed for every quarrel.

name: Lorgesse
blurb: Ferry village where river-guild toll-men and royal sergeants trade insults every day.

name: Dusmerc
blurb: Forest-edge village of charcoal burners who sell to whichever lord pays first.

name: Fontagne
blurb: Spring village with a stone well carved with the old kings' names, half scratched out.

name: Cazelune
blurb: Hunting village where the regents hold tournaments to prove which of them is bravest.

name: Brenvaud
blurb: Bridge village guarding the only dry crossing; its lord has never paid a toll himself.

name: Aurigol
blurb: Gold-dust village whose miners are paid in promissory notes from the empty treasury.

name: Teoulac
blurb: Fishing village on a mere; locals claim a drowned knight rings the bell at night.

name: Ymbrane
blurb: Hill village known for falconers, whose hawks are gifts exchanged between rival lords.

name: Sauvanesse
blurb: Monastery village whose scribes keep the realm's genealogies, and forge them when needed.

name: Quelmont
blurb: Quiet hamlet of salt-pan workers, fighting the river-guild over every bag they sell.

name: Tassemmar
blurb: Salt-weighing city whose brass scales set the weight for every caravan contract.

name: Ouarnast
blurb: Wharf town on the salt lake; rival caravans duel for the first place at the loading ramp.

name: Ahnarou
blurb: Oasis market where date groves feed caravans before the long waste crossing.

name: Imzellan
blurb: Walled well-town; its Dry Gate shuts each year on the first sandstorm of autumn.

name: Iggoudar
blurb: Toll-castle at the river ford; its garrison has fought the Regency for a decade.

name: Azzenwar
blurb: Hilltop well-fort guarding the only spring on the northern salt road.

name: Tahnoun
blurb: Mud-brick keep where the clans hold their oath-moots under the stars.

name: Amrash
blurb: Watchtower of pale stone where lookouts signal raids by mirror and smoke.

name: Irhessa
blurb: Ruined fort said to be built by the first salt-kings, haunted by their camels.

name: Ouallen
blurb: Strong gatehouse over the caravan route; any lancer who passes owes it a song.

name: Iddrin
blurb: Date-farmers' hamlet known for the sweetest fruit in the south.

name: Tamzerat
blurb: Well village where a legend says the first camel knelt to drink.

name: Ahlouf
blurb: Tent-camp that moves with the seasons and never shows its walls twice.

name: Essidra
blurb: Salt-pan village; its workers sing a grudge against river-guild buyers.

name: Unzal
blurb: Dust-bowl hamlet of goatherds, famous for its rough wine of figs.

name: Tifrasht
blurb: Shrine-spring where caravaners leave a coin and a promise for safe passage.

name: Imzaz
blurb: Mint village that stamps the clans' silver tokens for trade.

name: Anhilt
blurb: Hamlet of tanners who cure hides for the lancers' saddles and boots.

name: Tazirda
blurb: Horse-breeding village whose grey mares are prized across the continent.

name: Ouzmar
blurb: Quarry hamlet cutting pale stone for the few castles the clans raise.

name: Ifghelen
blurb: Oasis village with a sunken garden said to hold a sleeping spirit.

name: Tinouzat
blurb: Shepherd village; its herders still nurse the grudge of a stolen flock.

name: Ahnazz
blurb: Caravanserai village where a neutral oath is sworn over a bowl of salt.

name: Irzaghen
blurb: Mud village built on the bones of a raided fort, a warning to raiders.

name: Tahassal
blurb: Village of falconers whose birds hunt the Fen's reed-geese each autumn.

name: Ilmadd
blurb: Lamp village known for oil pressed from desert seeds and sold in the towns.
